title: An AI-Native 3D game engine
author: Flaky-Mail-2889
selftext:
Hi all,

I'm working on a holistic platform to generate 3D assets and full games using AI. As I'd like to put it, it's an AI-native 3D game engine, built for people with great ideas — so they can produce a game without the barrier of money or deep technical knowledge, only great taste.

I used to have my own 3D company a few years ago. I've collected a lot of data and trained my own 3D generative model based on real artists' work (for which they were paid). My 3D asset generation is quite on par with the big players, simply because of the quality of the data I've collected.

Would this be something you'd be willing to try once we come out of stealth?

We're not able to offer it for free, as we're a stealth startup without funding yet, nor credits from cloud providers. However, I can offer a 50% discount — the price points are €16 and €50, so it would be €8 and €25.

Would that be something you'd be willing to spend to test it out?

comments.author: blingsdubai
comments.body:
This is actually pretty interesting, especially the part about the whole pipeline. I think generating the asset is only one piece of the problem and getting it into a usable state and then actually integrating it into a game is where things get messy pretty quickly.  
  
There are already tools like Meshy that can generate pretty good assets and provide API access, but I think the more interesting challenge is what happens after generation. When you’re dealing with hundreds or thousands of assets, how do you reliably get them from generated to “actually usable in the game” without the workflow becoming a bottleneck?
